definitions.gloss: outline; brief portrayal (of a person, situation, or era)
definitions.explanation: outline; brief portrayal (of a person, situation, or era)

examples.japanese: {鉛筆|えんぴつ}で{素描|そびょう}する。
{美術|びじゅつ}{教室|きょうしつ}で{人物|じんぶつ}の{素描|そびょう}を{練習|れんしゅう}した。
examples.english: I practiced figure sketching in art class.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{素描|そびょう}は{線|せん}が{繊細|せんさい}で{美|うつく}しい。
examples.english: His sketches have delicate, beautiful lines.

examples.japanese: {時代|じだい}の{素描|そびょう}を{試|こころ}みる。
examples.english: To attempt a sketch of the era.

examples.japanese: この{小説|しょうせつ}は{戦後|せんご}の{人々|ひとびと}の{暮|く}らしを{素描|そびょう}している。
examples.english: This novel sketches the lives of people in the postwar period.

examples.japanese: {著者|ちょしゃ}は{庶民|しょみん}の{日常|にちじょう}を{素描|そびょう}することで、{社会|しゃかい}の{変化|へんか}を{浮|う}き{彫|ぼ}りにした。
examples.english: By sketching the daily lives of ordinary people, the author brought social change into relief.

notes:
In its literal sense, refers to a drawing made with simple materials like pencil or charcoal, without color. In its figurative sense, means to give a brief, evocative portrayal of something in writing.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {人物|じんぶつ}{素描|そびょう}: figure sketch; character sketch
- {素描|そびょう}{帳|ちょう}: sketchbook
- {木炭|もくたん}{素描|そびょう}: charcoal sketch
- {時代|じだい}の{素描|そびょう}: sketch of an era

SIMILAR WORDS:
- スケッチ: sketch — the loanword equivalent; more casual and widely used in everyday conversation
- デッサン: dessin — specifically refers to academic drawing exercises focusing on form and proportion
- {下書|したが}き: rough draft — refers to a preliminary version of writing or drawing, not a finished sketch
